articles.title: Weather on the board today
articles.body:
A dense high-pressure system of political speculation settled over the morning, centered on who would inherit Modi’s chair.

The air was thick with name-dropping and low-visibility arguments about Yogi’s odds, creating a stagnant atmosphere that lasted until lunch. As the sun climbed, a scattered drizzle of caste anxiety began to fall.

One front brought news of a Jat IPS officer dumping his wife, which quickly turned into a localized storm of gendered insults.

Another cell of precipitation formed around the term 'Abbos,' where Anon cycled through defensive rants about global racism. The rain was persistent, though light.

By evening, the pressure dropped entirely into a low-hanging fog of obscene promotion. Anon used profanity to advertise the BHIM UPI app, while separate threads circulated college rumors wrapped in graphic sexual boasts.

The sky remained overcast with bad faith, offering no clear break until the lights went out.

articles.title: Anons Dispute Yogi's Viability as Modi's Successor
articles.body:
Anon on /b/ asked who would succeed Narendra Modi in the BJP and who they wanted to see in that role, even if unlikely.

The replies immediately fractured into arguments about state-level dynamics, caste politics, and the perceived decline of the party's central narrative. One Anon argued that Yogi Adityanath is the primary contender but faces internal resistance.

They claimed the BJP organization views Yogi as a threat to the party’s broader social hierarchy, noting that senior leaders in the same line for the PM seat have not shown interest in backing him.

This Anon suggested that the party only announces Chief Minister candidates late to manage these internal frictions, implying that Yogi’s radical stance clashes with the pragmatic, win-at-all-costs ideology that defined Modi’s earlier career.

Another respondent countered that Yogi’s radicalism is a liability because he is not RSS-affiliated and sends the wrong signal to southern India, though they admitted he is not yet disqualified.

Critics of the current leadership asserted that the "magic era" of development and anti-corruption rhetoric is over.

One poster declared that economic growth has stagnated and the "Make in India" initiative has failed, referring to the country as "Lundia" and Modi as a weak coward who bent to rural, caste-based demands.

They argued that Modi’s failure to deliver on 2014 and 2019 promises has cost the party its majority, and that the "Chodi" meme, a derogatory term for Modi, died in 2024 because the reality is worse than the caricature.

A different Anon suggested that Yogi, Amit Shah, or similar figures are not suitable for appealing to young voters post-protest, arguing that the party needs a new face to survive the next cycle. Supporters of the ruling party dismissed these assessments as delusional.

One Anon stated that to think BJP will lose all elections is to live in a delusion, pointing out that dynamics change every five years and every state.

They argued that BJP’s strategy of winning state elections is intact and that opponents are merely explaining away losses with excuses.

Another poster noted that while West Bengal was a lost cause due to TMC goons, Haryana runs on Jaat vs. non-Jaat caste politics, and Maharashtra is complicated by the weakened Shiv Sena under Uddhav Thackeray.

They argued that rural India does not vote on Hindu-Muslim binaries, making the urban focus of the criticism irrelevant to the majority of the electorate.

Among potential successors, Shivraj Singh Chouhan was named by one Anon as a strong candidate, citing his massive, organic rural voter base built through welfare schemes and his moderate, seasoned presence.

Another Anon wrote down a prediction that it would be either Chouhan or Dev Fadnavis, dismissing Yogi as "too much orange." A separate thread of discussion focused on the structural flaw of the Indian parliamentary system, with one Anon noting that as the largest minority, winning 30% of votes in 500 seats can yield a majority, a mechanism they described as retarded compared to proportional representation systems in Europe.

The thread ended without consensus, with Anons continuing to argue over whether the next election result will be a mere formality or a genuine reckoning for the party’s leadership.

articles.title: Jat IPS Officer Allegedly Dumps Wife After Civil Service Success
articles.body:
Anon claimed that a woman referred to as a Bamani was crying after being dumped by a Jat IPS officer who had just secured a position in the civil services.

The initial post framed the breakup as a predictable outcome of the man’s rise in status, suggesting he had used the relationship to support his UPSC preparation before discarding her. Replyers quickly challenged the cast ascribed in the original post.

One anon corrected the record, stating that the officer, named Bhanu Pratap Singh, was actually Rajput, not Jat. Another respondent insisted the man was indeed Jat and directed others to check news articles.

A third anon intervened to stop the debate, calling for the discussion to drop the matter, while another noted that the woman was from a Brahmin family in Kolkata and had worked as a teacher in Bharatpur for five years.

Despite the factual corrections, the thread pivoted toward broader caste narratives. Anon described the situation as a common humiliation for “pongas” and predicted the same fate for liberal groups.

One poster joked about the magic in the situation, musing about whether he should pursue a similar strategy to achieve IAS status.

Others used the incident to discuss political dynamics, with one anon stating that the BJP kept winning regardless of these personal disputes, while another claimed Rajput communities were trying to steal political glory. The conversation remained filled with profanity and derogatory terminology throughout.

Multiple posters used slurs like “randirakshak” and “Bantu nigger” to describe various groups, including historical references to the Delhi Sultanate.

One anon accused the woman of living large on the man’s money, while another argued that trapping a “smart or higher class pongi” was the fastest way to success.

The thread ended with mixed opinions on the man’s caste and the woman’s background, with no consensus reached on the specific details of the relationship.

articles.title: Lumping All Indians as 'Abbos'
articles.body:
Anon asked on the board why there is so much racism against India. The immediate response was a list of physical and cultural defects. One anon claimed Indians are physically weak, mentally weak, dark, short, and filthy.

They cited open-air defecation and the smell of spices as primary grievances, adding that Indian religious rituals are backward and cause problems for everyone. Another reply mocked the OP's question by adopting a caricatured accent.

This anon suggested the hate exists because Indians are "CEO saar" and because of a perceived genetic or cultural gap, writing that the OP did not get the satire. A separate thread of replies focused on internal racial hierarchy.

One anon argued that North Indian upper castes are genetically closer to white people than to darker-skinned South Indians, noting that some North Indians can pass as European or Persian.

Another anon disputed this, stating that the average North Indian upper caste is much closer to the darker population than to Persians, let alone whites.

Several anons took issue with the generalization, pointing out that the traits listed as negative, such as being dark or short, apply only to a specific subset of the population.

They noted that this subset makes up 90% of the population, effectively making "Indians" and "Abbos" synonymous in the eyes of the board.

The thread ended with a consensus that the average Indian male has just as many sexual partners as the average white male, dispelling one common stereotype.

The interaction remained focused on genetic lineage and caste distinctions rather than addressing the initial question about the origin of the prejudice.

articles.title: Anonymous Uses Profanity to Promote BHIM UPI
articles.body:
An Anon posted a vulgar Hindi obscenity directed at Modi and followed it with "namo namo" and the BHIM Janta Party logo. The post attempted to frame the payment app as a political tool.

A respondent replied that free transactions were available on BHIM UPI. Another Anon countered that the service was not free and suggested that users send money to a BHIM account to make arrangements.

A final reply simply stated "jai bhim." The thread ended without resolving the question of transaction fees.

articles.title: Caste Porn and College Rumors
articles.body:
Anon posted a crude boast about Jaat virility, prompting a pile-on of caste-based insults and unverified claims. Respondents immediately attacked the OP’s identity, labeling him a "dehati" projecting a false image.

They claimed a granddaughter of a politician slept with a local man at an NCR college, a rumor offered without proof.

Others dismissed the OP as a fake, noting he was actually admin of a Jaat page.

The thread quickly devolved into generic insults, with Anons exchanging obscenities and denying any basis for the initial post. No facts were established in the exchange.
